stem: A heart waitlist candidate is placed on inactive status while temporarily unsuitable for transplant. According to OPTN Policy 3.6.A, how does waiting time accrue during inactivity?

options.text: No waiting time accrues while the candidate remains inactive
Unlimited waiting time accrues, as for kidney candidates
Waiting time accrues only for the first 30 cumulative inactive days
Waiting time doubles each week the candidate remains inactive

explanation.rationale_correct: OPTN Table 3-3 specifies that heart candidates accrue no waiting time while inactive, unlike kidney candidates who accrue unlimited inactive waiting time.

rationale_incorrect.B: Unlimited inactive accrual applies to kidney candidates, not heart candidates.
rationale_incorrect.C: A 30-day cumulative inactive accrual limit applies to intestine candidates, not heart candidates.
rationale_incorrect.D: Heart inactive waiting time does not double weekly; it does not accrue at all.

primary_anchor.section: Policy 3.6.A → Table 3-3 Waiting Time for Inactive Candidates → Heart
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Heart … No time … Candidates accrue waiting time while inactive

references.locator: Policy 3.6.A → Table 3-3: Waiting Time for Inactive Candidates (heart candidates accrue no waiting time while inactive); PDF p. 46 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Seventh 020500 item; heart inactive waiting-time angle paired with kidney unlimited accrual (cctc-2037); anchor verified on optn-policies p. 46.

stem: After evaluation is complete, the interdisciplinary team determines a candidate will not be registered on the waitlist at this time. What OPTN-required communication must the program provide?

options.text: Written notification within 10 business days that evaluation is complete and the patient will not be registered on the waiting list at this time
No written notice because only approved candidates receive any communication
Automatic waitlist registration despite the team's determination
Verbal notice only after an organ offer is generated

explanation.rationale_correct: OPTN Policy 3.5 requires written notification within 10 business days when evaluation is complete and the patient will not be registered on the waiting list at this time.

rationale_incorrect.B: Policy 3.5 explicitly requires written notification for completed evaluations that do not result in waitlist registration.
rationale_incorrect.C: The team's determination not to register must be communicated rather than overridden by automatic listing.
rationale_incorrect.D: Written notification is required at evaluation conclusion, not deferred until organ offer.

primary_anchor.section: Policy 3.5 → Table 3-2 → evaluation complete, not registered
primary_anchor.quote_hint: evaluation has been completed and the patient will not be registered on the waiting list at this time

references.locator: Policy 3.5 → Table 3-2 (written notification when evaluation complete and patient not registered on waiting list); PDF p. 46 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Seventh 020400 item; OPTN not-registered notification distinct from registration notice (cctc-2041) and not-listed counseling (cctc-2017); anchor verified on optn-policies p. 46.

stem: A waitlisted candidate changes health insurance and moves to a new address. What is the candidate's responsibility per standard waitlist management references?

options.text: Notify the transplant team of changes in health insurance and contact information
Update insurance and address only with the organ procurement organization, not the transplant program
Withhold all changes until after transplantation occurs
Automatic delisting occurs without any requirement to notify the team

explanation.rationale_correct: Waitlist management includes patient responsibility to notify the transplant team of changes in health status, health insurance, and contact information such as address and phone numbers.

rationale_incorrect.B: The transplant team must be notified directly about insurance and contact changes affecting waitlist management.
rationale_incorrect.C: Insurance and contact changes should be reported promptly while waitlisted, not deferred until after transplant.
rationale_incorrect.D: Candidates are expected to notify the team; changes do not automatically delist without program review.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 3, Patient Education → §9. Waitlist management → b.i.
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Notify the transplant team of any changes in their Health insurance Contact information (address, phone numbers)

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 3 → §9. Waitlist management → b.i. (notify team of health insurance and contact information changes); PDF p. 101 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Seventh 020600 item; waitlist insurance/contact reporting distinct from health-status admissions (cctc-2042) and donor disclosure (cctc-2039); anchor verified on Cupples p. 101.

stem: When summarizing evaluation outcomes for a candidate with life-threatening intestinal failure, which transplant option is recognized as standard of care in the United States?

options.text: Intestine transplantation for adults and children with life-threatening intestinal failure
Intestine transplantation is experimental and never performed in the United States
Lifetime total parenteral nutrition without any surgical option
Isolated cosmetic abdominal surgery without transplant evaluation

explanation.rationale_correct: Intestine transplantation was recognized in 2000 as the standard of care for adults and children with life-threatening intestinal failure in the United States.

rationale_incorrect.B: Intestine transplantation is an established standard of care rather than a prohibited experimental procedure in the United States.
rationale_incorrect.C: Intestine transplantation is indicated when long-term parenteral nutrition cannot adequately treat intestinal failure.
rationale_incorrect.D: Cosmetic surgery is not the standard-of-care option for life-threatening intestinal failure.

primary_anchor.quote_hint: recognized in 2000 as the standard of care for adults and children with life-threatening intestinal failure

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 13 → Introduction → A. (intestine transplantation standard of care for life-threatening intestinal failure); PDF p. 679 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Seventh 020300 item; second intestine-organ tag; standard-of-care framing distinct from long-term TPN outcomes (cctc-3013); anchor verified on Cupples p. 679.
